question: Which among the following is the official sport of Maharashtra, as of 2022?
solution:
The correct answer is **Dahi-Handi**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Maharashtra State officially recognised Dahi Handi as an adventure sport.
 
• The participants, known as Govindas, will be recognised as athletes.
 
• Dahi Handi is an occasion connected to the Hindu festival of Krishna Janmashtami in Maharashtra.
 
• It involves earthen pots filled with yoghurt. In this game, "Govindas" dons colorful clothing and builds a human pyramid to shatter the hanging pot.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__****Kalaripayattu:**

 
• Kalaripayattu is a martial art.
 
• It originated in Kerala from the 3rd century BC to the 2nd century AD.
 
• The place where this martial art is practised is called a 'Kalari'.
 
• It is considered to be among the oldest martial arts still in existence.

Mallakamb:

 
• A Traditional Indian sport, Mallakamb involves a gymnast performing feats with a vertical wooden pole or rope. 
 
• The word, Mallakamb, also refers to the pole used in the sport.
 
• The word ‘Mallakhamb’ comes from coalescing two words- ‘malla’ meaning wrestler and ‘ khamb’ meaning pole.
 
• The gymnast performs aerial yoga postures on a wooden pole, a cane, or simply a rope.
 
• Traditionally, a wooden pole is used to perform yoga postures, which are made of Sheesham or Indian Rosewood and smoothened by castor oil. 
 
• Over the years, three types of mallakhamb variations have gained popularity in competitions.
 
• They are pole mallakhamb, hanging mallakhamb, and rope mallakhamb.
 
• Pole mallakhamb is essentially the traditional form of mallakhamb.
 
• Competitors perform on a wooden pole that is 2.6m in height and has a circumference of 55cm at the base.
 
• The pole gradually tapers to a circumference of 35cm at the top.
 
• Hanging mallakhamb, meanwhile, uses a shorter pole suspended with hooks or chains as the prop.
 
• The bottom of the pole in the hanging mallakhamb doesn’t touch the ground.
 
• Rope mallakhamb is performed on a suspended rope that is 5.5m long and 2cm in diameter.​
